tasks.title: interactions: zone-rule classifier v0 over frame JSONL
tasks.goal: Turn ObservationFrame JSONL into InteractionEvent JSONL with hand-tuned zone rules and event segmentation. This is the always-available classifier everything else falls back to (invariant 7).
acceptance: `uv run python -m kitchen.interactions.events --frames <frames.jsonl> --zones <zones.json> --out events.jsonl` works end to end

Rules in kitchen/interactions/zone_rules.py: a tool inside a bin_slot with overlap and dwell near a wrist is transfer.scoop (bin to tool). Sustained overlap of a hand or tool with a plate or bin is transfer.contact (both). Sustained moving overlap across a plate is transfer.wipe (both). Dwell in the wash zone is clean.wash as a self-loop (a_id == b_id)
The segmenter in kitchen/interactions/events.py merges per-frame hits into events with t_start_ms <= t_end_ms and deterministic event_ids, emitted in t_start_ms order per pair (`safety` test)

Every expected event in the interactions-02 fixtures is matched within 200 ms, and the near-miss fixture yields no event with probability >= 0.5: `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k rules_fixtures`
clean.wash needs the wash zone, a minimum dwell and probability at or above the wash floor. A `safety` test shows a brief pass through the wash zone yields no wash
Every output line validates against interaction_event, with classifier {name: zone_rules, version}
All rule constants live in one config object, are logged at startup, and are encoded in classifier.version

tasks.title: interactions: hand-written frame fixtures with expected events
tasks.goal: Unblock rule development before vision-01 lands, with tiny, readable frame JSONL scenes whose correct events are known.
acceptance: At least 4 fixtures under kitchen/interactions/tests/fixtures/frames/: a knife scoop from a bin slot, a hand touching a plate, a tool dwelling in the wash zone, and a near miss (a tool passes over a plate without dwelling)

Each fixture has 30 frames or fewer, validates against observation_frame (every detection carries origin), and has a sibling <name>.expected.json listing the expected events (action, pair, direction, approximate t_start_ms and t_end_ms)
A matching zones.json fixture with bin_slot, plating_spot, wash and clean_stack zones
`uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k fixtures_valid` passes

tasks.title: interactions: candidate pairs and allergen-blind features
tasks.goal: Generate candidate pairs (hand-tool, tool-bin, tool-plate, hand-bin, hand-plate) and compute InteractionFeatures per pair per frame, with no path for allergen information to leak in (invariant 6).
acceptance: kitchen/interactions/candidates.py generates only the five pair types, within a configurable distance or overlap. Unit tests cover each pair type and the cutoff

kitchen/interactions/features.py uses distance and speeds in normalized frame widths (per second), overlap as intersection over the smaller box, inside_zone, zone_kind (never the zone ID), dwell_ms, and wrist_proximity or null
Every feature row validates against interaction_features (additionalProperties false): `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k features_contract`
`safety` import-lint test: nothing in kitchen/interactions imports or reads bin_profile, entity_risk, allergen units or StateClient allergen reads
`safety` property test: features are identical whatever the bin allergen profiles are
Features are stable, within tolerance, across 15, 30 and 60 FPS resamplings of the same scene

tasks.title: interactions: ADR on edge direction (OQ-9)
tasks.goal: Settle which way allergens move on each action. The partner's graph propagates along these directions, so the partner must agree.
acceptance: An ADR PR in docs/decisions/ covers contact and wipe as both ways, scoop as bin to tool, and wash as a self-loop (already documented in the interaction_event schema), with the alternatives considered
An owner:partner issue asks the partner to ACK, and their ACK is linked from the ADR
The verdict Manager is told on their Team board, since chains are explained along these directions
OQ-9 is marked for the Director to move to Resolved once merged

tasks.title: interactions: publish recorded event JSONL fixture pack
tasks.goal: Ship the fake that verdict, the partner graph and the e2e harness test against: event JSONL produced by the real zone-rule classifier on known scenes.
acceptance: At least 4 event fixtures under kitchen/interactions/tests/fixtures/events/, generated by kitchen.interactions.events from the interactions-02 frames. The regeneration command is in the README
Every line validates against interaction_event
A test regenerates them and fails on drift: `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k event_pack_fresh`
Announced on the verdict and platform Team boards, plus an owner:partner issue with the paths

tasks.title: interactions: classifier wrapper that always lands on zone rules
tasks.goal: kitchen/interactions/classifier.py wraps an optional primary classifier (the partner's LSTM, once adopted) so that a load failure, exception or timeout falls back to zone rules, and every event names the classifier that produced it (invariant 7).
acceptance: zone_rules and the wrapper both implement the InteractionClassifier Protocol
`safety` tests using platform's ScriptedClassifier as the primary: missing, raising or past-the-timeout yields zone_rules output, with classifier.name = zone_rules on the event
A healthy primary's events carry its own name and version
Which primary to use is config only, defaulting to none (zone rules). The LSTM slot points at kitchen.lstm only after the M3 adoption ADR
Fallbacks are logged and counted, and the count is exposed for health. `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -m safety` passes

tasks.title: interactions: streaming pipeline writing edges via StateClient
tasks.goal: Consume ObservationFrames in-process from vision, emit events incrementally, and write them through StateClient.record_interactions within 500 ms of event end, never dropping one silently.
acceptance: kitchen/interactions/events.py accepts a frame iterator (in-process on the Pi, or JSONL replay) and emits events as segments close
Event end to record_interactions within 500 ms, measured with FixedClock in a test
Batched writes with deterministic, idempotent event_ids. Replaying the same frames twice writes no duplicates
`safety` test: on StateUnavailable, events are buffered and retried, and none are lost once the fake recovers. Buffer depth is exposed for health
Fake-swap test: frame fixtures through the pipeline into InMemoryStateClient match the event pack: `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k pipeline_e2e`
out_of_scope: Real SpacetimeDB on the Pi (M2, partner database)

tasks.title: interactions: tune rules on vision's recorded frame pack
tasks.goal: Move from hand-written frames to vision's recorded fixture pack (kitchen/vision/tests/fixtures/pack/, published after vision-01), label the expected events, and lock them in as a regression suite.
acceptance: Expected-event files for each scene in vision's pack, committed under kitchen/interactions/tests/fixtures/
Rules re-tuned, with constants changed only in the config object. The PR shows matches and misses before and after
Regression test `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k recorded_pack` passes with no missed expected transfer and no false clean.wash
The scene where a tool leaves and re-enters produces events on the new entity ID only, never the old one

tasks.title: interactions: labeled clip dataset format and validator
tasks.goal: Define how real recordings and their labels are stored and split, so the owner can start recording (OQ-12), the partner can train, and the benchmark can't leak.
acceptance: An ADR in docs/decisions/ covers the session layout (vision recorder manifest, frames.jsonl, and labels.jsonl with pair, action, direction, t_start_ms, t_end_ms, labeler) and a split policy by session, never by clip. The partner ACKs on an owner:partner issue
`uv run python -m kitchen.interactions.labels validate <dir>` checks the layout, label validity against frames, and overlaps
A held-out manifest format with a content hash, so the held-out set can be frozen
A tiny labeled sample session (100 KB or less) committed under kitchen/interactions/tests/fixtures/ passes validation
An owner-facing recording guide posted on the issue: what to film, for how long, and how to name it

tasks.title: interactions: labeling tool v0 for candidate segments
tasks.goal: Let a person label actions quickly by stepping through candidate-pair segments from a recorded session, writing labels.jsonl in the dataset format.
acceptance: `uv run python -m kitchen.interactions.labels label --session <dir>` steps through candidate segments, takes one keypress per action (contact, scoop, wipe, wash, unimportant, skip), and writes labels.jsonl
Shows the video frame with both boxes when video is available, and falls back to a text view otherwise
Output passes the interactions-09 validator: `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k labeling_output`
Resumable: re-running skips segments already labeled

tasks.title: interactions: benchmark harness with cost-weighted score
tasks.goal: A frozen, reproducible way to compare any InteractionClassifier with zone rules on held-out labeled sessions. It decides whether the partner's LSTM is adopted in M3 (invariant 7).
acceptance: `uv run python -m kitchen.interactions.benchmark --classifier zone_rules --heldout <manifest>` writes report.json and report.md. --classifier also accepts a module path, so the partner can point it at kitchen.lstm
Event-level matching with temporal IoU, and per-action precision and recall
A cost-weighted score where a missed transfer and a false clean.wash carry the heaviest weights. The weights are documented in the interactions-09 ADR and shared with the partner
Refuses to run if the held-out manifest hash doesn't match the frozen one
Runs on the sample session in CI: `uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k benchmark_smoke`

tasks.title: interactions: export per-pair feature windows for LSTM training
tasks.goal: Produce the partner's LSTM training input: time-ordered windows of InteractionFeatures per pair, in a format sim can also generate synthetically.
acceptance: `uv run python -m kitchen.interactions.features export-windows --frames <jsonl> --out windows.jsonl --len <n> --stride <k>` writes one window per line
Every row in every window validates against interaction_features, and a window never mixes pairs
The window spec (length, stride, padding) is agreed on an owner:partner issue, documented in the README, and shared on the sim Team board
`uv run pytest kitchen/interactions -k windows` covers boundaries and short tracks
